title: Can’t Follow a Metronome? Start with One Short Phrase
description: If you cannot follow a metronome, start by tapping with its clicks, then play one short phrase at a manageable tempo.
direct: If you cannot follow a metronome, start by tapping with its clicks, then play one short phrase at a manageable tempo. Adding the whole song immediately gives you more things to coordinate than listening to the pulse alone.

cards.choice.heading: Make the task smaller
cards.choice.body: Choose a phrase you already know. Listen for a few beats, tap along, then say or clap the rhythm before playing. If you repeatedly rush or stop, simplify the phrase before increasing speed.
sections.explain.heading: A click is a reference
sections.explain.body: BPM describes beats per minute; it does not decide which note value you should count. Use the pulse indicated by your score or teacher. Avoid changing the beat interpretation and speed at the same time, since you may accidentally make the task twice as fast.
sections.practice.heading: Use recordings separately
sections.practice.body: Space Sheep Studio develops Audio Compressor MP3 Converter for iPhone. Its current release includes metronome, pitch and tempo tools. Changing a recording’s tempo and following a metronome are different practice tasks; use whichever addresses the obstacle. Export tools require Pro. No automatic rhythm assessment, performance scoring or guaranteed learning speed is claimed. Save your source recordings and keep listening to your own playing.

steps.step-1.text: Open the metronome tool in Audio Compressor MP3 Converter and choose a comfortable BPM using the available controls.
steps.step-2.text: Tap with the pulse first. Play one short phrase while keeping the clicks audible. Stop and restart deliberately when the pulse gets lost.
steps.step-3.text: Write down the tempo at which the phrase stays steady. Increase gradually only when several repetitions feel controlled.
